newsitem.title: USA: Edison protests Enova, PET merger.
newsitem.headline: Edison protests Enova, PET merger.

text.p: Edison International, the parent of Southern California Edison Co, filed a formal protest to the proposed merger between Enova Corp and Pacific Enterprises, the company said Thursday.
The filing, which was expected, was made to the California Public Utilities Commission, which is set to begin its review of the merger next year.

Enova's main subsidiary is San Diego Gas and Electric Co, while Southern California Gas Co, the main supplier of natural gas to Edison's electricity customers, is the primary unit of Pacific Enterprises.
Edison said the merger would increase vertical integration in the energy services market, potentially undermining the competitive marketplace envisioned for the state.
Enova and Pacific Enterprises announced in October plans to merge, creating the largest utility, in terms of customers, in the United States.

Analysts said the merger presents a direct threat to Edison's dominance of the Southern California electricity market, which along with the rest of the state, will begin opening utilities' monopoly territories to other competitors starting in January 1998.
